tasks.description: MEASURE the over-assignment on the real repo before changing anything. Scan src/ through the live scanner path and record: how many elements carry an imports array, how many of those reference NONE of the listed specifiers in their own body, and the mean imports-per-element. This is the measured_baseline; do not author the fix from the ticket summary. Note both assignment sites exist: tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:102 (TS/TSX path) and tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:146 (JS/JSX path). A fix that lands on one is half a fix.

ENUMERATE every reader of element.imports and record what each one would do under a narrowed field. Known readers: src/query/clones.ts:247+382 (importSources; :247 gates triviality so today NO element in a file with imports is ever trivial - a concrete wrong answer, and the strongest argument for narrowing), src/semantic/projections.ts:161, src/semantic/orchestrator.ts:280, src/scanner/semantic-analyzer.ts:68+126+129 (dedupe-and-merge with fileImports), src/pipeline/generators/context-generator.ts:1227, src/pipeline/semantic-elements.ts:28 (normalizeImportsField), src/scanner/scanner.ts:672 (winner.imports ?? loser.imports). Confirm the count first-hand; the source comment claims six and this task exists to verify that, not to repeat it.

DECIDE the narrowing rule and RECORD it in communication.json decisions_log before editing. The candidates: (a) keep only imports whose specifiers appear in the element body, (b) keep only imports the element's own calls resolve to, (c) leave the field whole-file but rename it so the name stops lying. Each consumer from P1-T2 must be checked against the chosen rule. HALT AND REPORT with named options if any two consumers require incompatible semantics - do not pick one and absorb the conflict silently. That disagreement is the same defect class this residue came from.

APPLY the ruled narrowing at BOTH sites - tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:102 and :146 - and replace the KNOWN, OUT OF SCOPE comment at :96 with what the field now means. Keep the TS and JS paths behaviourally identical; they diverging is how this class of defect starts.

CORRECT the stale docblock at src/pipeline/extractors/relationship-extractor.ts:116-118. It still asserts that ctx.calls feeds straight into the canonical graph builder and that changing source semantics globally would move the graph. Commit 8d54d37 corrected that claim in tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:77-85 only: resolve-tail.ts:47 builds a SEED graph, and constructGraphPhase at resolve-tail.ts:109 Object.assigns canonical nodes/edges over it from extractRawCalls, whose RawCallFact.scopePath is a string[] and never lost the enclosing class. Two comments on one seam, disagreeing - fix the one that was missed and state the narrower true reason the qualifyScopes default stays off (not re-specifying a legacy seam, NOT protecting the canonical graph).

AUTHOR a contract test that pins per-element imports on BOTH the TS and JS scanner paths, including an element that references no imports at all and one file where two elements reference disjoint imports. Add the clones.ts triviality case: an element with no own imports in a file that has imports MUST be eligible for trivial. The test must exercise the real scanner entry point, not a reimplementation - a private copy of production logic in a test file is exactly what phase 6 of the predecessor WO had to delete.

PROVE the test earns its place: revert the P1-T4 source edit only, re-run the new test, and record which cases fail at HEAD and which pass. A test that stays green against the un-fixed source proves nothing. Restore the edit afterwards.

RUN tsc --noEmit and the full vitest suite. Record exact pass/skip/fail counts against the pre-phase baseline. Note vitest 4 rejects --reporter=basic and the resulting startup crash reads as a failure - confirm real test counts before calling anything a regression.

measured_baseline.method: Three throwaway probes driving the REAL scanner entry point (scanFileWithTreeSitter) over all 256 non-test .ts/.tsx files under src/, plus a direct grammar-level probe comparing the two import extractors on identical source. All probes deleted after measuring.

over_assignment.reading: The over-assignment is TOTAL and uniform: in all 203 files that have imports, every element carries a byte-identical copy of the whole file list. 11,578 import entries are attached where 203 file-level lists would carry the same information.

clones_triviality_impact.reading: clones.ts:247 gates triviality on paramNames==0 AND importSources==0. The whole-file assignment suppresses the flag on 1,071 elements that would otherwise qualify - a 6.5x understatement. This is the one MEASURED downstream consequence; it is a real wrong answer in a live query surface, not a latent risk.

BLOCKING_FINDING.claim: element.imports[].specifiers is DEAD DATA. It is declared, always emitted as [], and never populated for TypeScript. Same for .default and .namespace.
BLOCKING_FINDING.measured: 26 of 26 import entries across 4 importing files carried specifiers: [], default: absent, namespace: absent - including files whose source plainly contains `import { X } from ...`.
BLOCKING_FINDING.proof: Grammar-level probe on the identical 3-line source. `node.childForFieldName("import_clause")` returns NULL for all three import forms; `node.namedChildren.find(c => c.type === "import_clause")` returns the import_clause node. relationship-extractor.ts:1106 uses the FORMER, so the entire specifiers/default/namespace block at :1120-1144 is UNREACHABLE for TypeScript. Legacy extractImports returned {sourceFile,target,line} only; extractRawImports on the SAME source returned specifiers [alpha,beta], defaultImport Def, namespaceImport NS, plus typeOnly.
BLOCKING_FINDING.the_defect_class_again: TWO import extractors in ONE class. The raw-facts path at :467 carries a comment stating "tree-sitter-typescript exposes `import_clause` as an unnamed-field child rather than via childForFieldName, so look it up by type." That fix was never backported to the legacy path 640 lines below it. This is the THIRD instance of the same class in this codebase - two components disagreeing about one seam, one fixed and one not, with nothing testing the seam.
BLOCKING_FINDING.blast_radius_today: LOW and measured: NO consumer of element.imports reads .specifiers. Every `specifiers` reference in src/ outside the extractor is the separate Acorn-based js-call-detector (which populates its own) or a type declaration. The dead field currently harms nothing.
BLOCKING_FINDING.why_it_BLOCKS_this_phase: P1-T3 planned to narrow element.imports to the imports an element actually references. That rule needs specifier / default / namespace tokens to match against the element body. Those tokens do not exist in the data the scanner path produces. The plan assumed a field that is structurally empty.

consumers_verified_first_hand: src/query/clones.ts:247 (isTrivial) and :382 (clone signature) - reads source only
COUNT: 7 read sites across 7 modules. The source comment at tree-sitter-file-scan.ts:99 claimed "six consumers" - close, and now verified rather than repeated. NONE of them reads .specifiers.
extractImports_callers: src/pipeline/orchestrator.ts:462 - and :465 calls extractRawImports on the SAME node, so the orchestrator already computes the CORRECT data alongside the broken data. Same shape as the ctx.calls finding: a legacy seed layer beside a correct canonical one.

narrowing_rule_ruled.rule: An import is retained on an element when ANY of its bound local names (named specifiers, default, namespace alias) appears as a whole word in the element body span [line, endLine].
narrowing_rule_ruled.conservative_by_design: Keep-on-any-match. The two error directions are NOT symmetric: a false KEEP retains an unused import (harmless, and it is the status quo), while a false DROP discards an import the element genuinely uses (data loss). The rule therefore errs toward keeping.
narrowing_rule_ruled.known_limits: This is a TEXT heuristic, not symbol resolution. A name appearing only in a comment or string keeps its import; a symbol reached dynamically or by computed access may be dropped. Real resolution needs the symbol table, which is far larger than this phase. Recorded so no reader mistakes the heuristic for precision.
narrowing_rule_ruled.operator_accepted_tradeoff: Occasional retained-but-unused import, in exchange for fixing the measured 193-vs-1264 clones.ts triviality understatement.

surface_audit_P1_T10.headline: YES - this phase DOES reach both the CLI and the MCP surface, through the clones tool. That is a change in user-visible output, not an internal-only correction.

reaches_both_surfaces.why: element.imports is not merely READ by clones - it is part of the clone SIGNATURE KEY. clones.ts:382-385 builds sig = {kind, name, arity, params, imports} and keys groups on JSON.stringify([kind, name, arity, params, imports]). Before narrowing, the imports component was FILE-CONSTANT, so it contributed nothing to discrimination between two elements in the same file and over-discriminated between files. After narrowing it is per-element, so clone GROUPING changes, not just the triviality flag at :247.
reaches_both_surfaces.measured_triviality_effect: 193 -> 1264 elements eligible for the trivial flag.

plan_adjustments_needed.description: P1-T3 HALT fired as designed, and the operator ruled (A) REPAIR + NARROW on 2026-08-02. The plan assumed element.imports carried specifier/default/namespace tokens to narrow against. Measured: it does not - relationship-extractor.ts:1106 resolves import_clause via childForFieldName, which tree-sitter-typescript returns NULL for, so the block at :1120-1144 has never executed for TS. The repair is the lookup the SAME FILE already proves correct at :465-467, with a comment explaining exactly this. Phase 1 therefore gains a prerequisite edit it did not plan: repair the extractor, THEN narrow. This is not scope creep - it is the phase discovering that its stated work had an unmet precondition.
